_about: THE list of collections the local prod mirror syncs (scripts/local-mirror reads it through mirror-targets.js; services.DebugMirror reads it as DebugMirror.Collections). One entry per collection, each with why it is mirrored. A collection missing here reads as permanently EMPTY on a /debug page, not slowly-from-prod. A running mirror notices an edit within a minute and restarts its tailers. `tasks` is deliberately absent: it is a WRITE path (the /debug row's re-enrich enqueues for the real worker), so mirroring it would strand the work locally.

collections.name: movies
collections.why: The corpus table: the film rows (/debug), also read by `ReviewLabelsCli` (the answers' film links, the queue).

collections.name: screenings
collections.why: The corpus table's showtimes, stitched back into the film rows.

collections.name: movie_slots
collections.why: The per-cinema slot rows the corpus readers resolve beside `movies`. Missing, every /debug film rendered slot-less.

collections.name: enrichment_attempts
collections.why: The per-row expand: each rating source's last fetch.

collections.name: rating_cadence
collections.why: The per-row expand: each rating source's refresh cadence.

collections.name: web_movies
collections.why: The /debug/readmodel dump of what the serving app actually serves. Missing, the dump was blank for every non-boot country.

collections.name: web_screenings
collections.why: The /debug/readmodel dump's screenings.

collections.name: cinema_scrapes
collections.why: Backs no /debug page. Each cinema's last content-bearing scrape: the listing the client actually produced, before the corpus merge touched it, which is what you read when a scrape looks wrong and the corpus a local replay replays. Over the tunnel that read is the latency this mirror exists to remove.

collections.name: identity_model_families
collections.why: Backs no page: the model's decisions, read by `ReviewLabelsCli queue`, `scripts/identity-slice` and `scripts/listing-history`. ~190 MB over the five countries with the other identity collections (2026-10-06).

collections.name: identity_listings
collections.why: Backs no page: each venue's last scrape as the identity intake holds it (catalogue ids, screenings), read by `scripts/venue-replay` and `scripts/listing-history`.

collections.name: venue_pages
collections.why: Backs no page: each listing's own film page at its venue, read by `scripts/venue-replay`.

collections.name: tmdb_films
collections.why: Backs no page: the resolver's own TMDB record of each candidate film, for the candidates the corpus lacks; local identity investigations read it.

collections.name: identity_family_answers
collections.why: Backs no page: what the other film databases answered, and each candidate's TMDB poster paths filed beside the hashes, read by `scripts/identity-slice` (13 MB over the five countries, 2026-10-08).

collections.name: identity_traces
collections.why: Backs no page: each listing's trace (the evidence for and against the film it weighed, every rule's refusal), read by `scripts/identity-slice`, `scripts/label-lookup` and `scripts/listing-history`.

collections.name: identity_agreements
collections.why: Backs no page: the agreement stage's stored verdicts (the film each cluster's families agreed on, or a fill rule took). Prod state no recording holds, which `scripts/identity-slice --prod-mirror` reads so a slice decides, and explains, as prod's stage does.

collections.name: identity_history
collections.why: Backs no page: a month of the identity system's history -- every answer, venue page and listing the model read as it moved, every read that failed, every take moved with what decided it -- which `scripts/identity-replay` resolves a past moment from and `scripts/identity-why` explains a take change by.

collections.name: identity_agreement_keys
collections.why: Backs no page: the agreement stage's cluster keys, which its verdicts in `identity_agreements` are filed under, each with its cluster's first listing. `scripts/identity-slice --prod-mirror` reads them to find each cluster's stored verdict.

collections.name: identity_pins
collections.why: Backs no page: operator pins, read by `scripts/identity-slice --prod-mirror` beside the agreements.

collections.name: identity_staging
collections.why: The staging screen (/debug/identity/staging): each country's clusters still waiting on an answer and those resolved lately, capped by its publisher (at most 700 small documents a country).

collections.name: uptimeBuckets
collections.why: Backs no /debug page: ~24 h of 15-minute scrape outcomes per service (TTL-expired in prod; the tailer carries those deletes). The scheduled white-cinema investigation (docs/white-cinema-investigations.md) replays /uptime's classification over them, since /uptime is admin-gated and prod Mongo is off limits to agents.

collections.name: filmwebFallback
collections.why: Backs no /debug page: one document per venue that ever fell back (PL's own-site to Filmweb, UK chains to Flicks; other countries hold none, and an empty prod collection never makes a mirror stale). The white-cinema sweep reads it beside the buckets to tell a venue served via its fallback from one that is genuinely white.
